title: Grateful Dead Live at Stanley Theater on 1969-02-07
lineage: SBD > MC > DAT > HHb > CDR > EAC (secure) > CD Wave > Cool Edit Pro > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: High‑energy late‑show from ’69 captured on a soundboard tape; despite cassette hiss and heavy compression the performance dazzles with monster versions of The Other One, Alligator, Death Don't and an explosive Feedback jam.
ai_review.review: The show is hailed as one of the finest examples of early‑1969 Dead, delivering relentless energy, soaring guitar work from Jerry and powerful bass counter‑themes from Phil. While the source is a cassette master that suffers from hiss, compression and occasional fade‑ins/outs, the mix remains listenable and the musical moments – especially The Other One > Cryptical, Alligator, Death Don't and the Feedback suite – more than compensate for the technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews overwhelmingly praise the musical performance (average ~4.8/5) while noting consistent but moderate recording issues (average ~3.7/5); weighted average yields a strong 4.5 rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Cassette master with noticeable hiss, heavy compression making EQ difficult, and fade‑ins/fade‑outs; however the mix is clear enough to hear all instruments and vocals.

standout_songs: Death Don't Have a Bad Time
show_quality.setlist_flow: Late‑show set builds from a blistering opening into extended jams; transitions such as Alligator→Drums→Jam→Primal Alligator are praised for their fluidity and intensity.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly described as soaring, acid‑drenched, full of pyrotechnics and bluesy emotion; his tone is highlighted as a key driver of the show’s intensity.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for counter‑theme playing to Jerry and delivering a standout solo during the jam; bass work described as powerful and complementary.
band_member_comments.Bob: One reviewer felt Bob Weir's playing was weaker than usual on this night.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum segment is called fast, furious and explosive; "Pig" (Mickey Hart) delivers a stellar Alligator performance and the post‑drum jam receives high praise.
